title: Numerical normal generation on a projective nodal curve
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $X$ be a nonempty connected projective reduced $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-kun-projective, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Assume $X$ is smooth except at ordinary nodes, whose completed local rings are $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Suppose that for every nonempty reduced union $B$ of irreducible components of $X$, including disconnected unions and $B=X$, one has
$$\deg_k(L|_B)\geq 2p_a(B)+1,\qquad p_a(B):=1-\chi(B,\mathcal O_B),$$
using degree [def-pc-degree-line-bundle], Euler characteristic [def-pc-euler-characteristic], and module pullback for restriction [def-pc-module-pullback]. Then for every integer $j\geq1$ the multiplication map
$$\operatorname{Sym}^j_k H^0(X,L)\longrightarrow H^0(X,L^{\otimes j})$$
is surjective. The map is induced by tensor products of sections, with the multiplication convention of [def-sc-invertible-section-ring] and cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology].

source.place: Franciosi--Tenni, The canonical ring of a 3-connected curve, Rend. Lincei Mat. Appl. 25 (2014), 37--51, Section 4, Theorem 4.2, printed p.49; nodal specialization of the reduced planar-singularity theorem. Section 2, printed p.39, fixes arbitrary algebraically closed characteristic and the meaning of subcurve. Local PDF WANTED; author-hosted primary text read online.

proof.text: The projective morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], hence of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Invertible modules are locally free of rank one and quasi-coherent [def-sc-invertible-module], hence coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. We use the long exact sequence [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] for module-sheaf cohomology: its hypotheses hold by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives] and [lem-sc-global-sections-left-exact]. Every reduced closed subcurve is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper, lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition], so the same Noetherian and cohomology facts apply to it.

source.place: Franciosi--Tenni, The canonical ring of a 3-connected curve, Section 4, Theorem 4.2, printed p.49; primary author-hosted text read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: For any nonempty connected reduced subcurve $B$, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-reduced-algclosed-global-sections-product] gives $h^0(B,\mathcal O_B)=1$. Higher cohomology above degree one vanishes by [lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-above-dimension]; hence $p_a(B)=h^1(B,\mathcal O_B)\geq0$, using [def-pc-euler-characteristic]. Therefore $\deg(L|_B)\geq1$, and degree additivity [lem-trf-curve-degree-tensor-additive] gives $\deg(L^{\otimes r}|_B)=r\deg(L|_B)\geq2p_a(B)+1$ for $r\geq1$. Apply [lem-sfb-curve-ideal-h1-subcurve-obstruction] with the empty subscheme: nonzero $H^1(X,L^{\otimes r})$ would give such a $B$ with degree at most $2p_a(B)-2$, a contradiction. Thus $H^1(X,L^{\otimes r})=0$ for every $r\geq1$.

source.place: Franciosi--Tenni, The canonical ring of a 3-connected curve, Section 4, Theorem 4.2, printed p.49; primary author-hosted text read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Let $x$ be a reduced closed point of $X$. Its residue field is $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base]. For every reduced subcurve $B$, the intersection $x\times_XB$ is empty or this reduced point, hence has length at most one. Nonzero $H^1(X,I_x\otimes L)$ would, by [lem-sfb-curve-ideal-h1-subcurve-obstruction], give $\deg(L|_B)\leq 2p_a(B)-1$, contradicting the hypothesis. Thus this $H^1$ vanishes. Tensoring the defining ideal quotient sequence with $L$ is exact by [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf, lem-sc-ext-tensor-exact]. Its cohomology sequence (Step 1) gives surjectivity $V=H^0(X,L)\to L\otimes k(x)$. Thus some global section is nonzero at each closed point. Also $V$ is finite-dimensional by the proper coherent cohomology theorem [lem-pc-coherent-hi].

source.place: Theorem 4.2, first sentence (Proposition 2.5); only base-point-freeness and H1 are needed outside the general-section cluster lemma. Stacks Tag 0E3E (curves.tex lemma-vanishing-on-gorenstein) supplies these directly.

proof.text: Choose $s$ and $S=Z(s)$ by [lem-sfb-general-section-cluster-strict-bound]. They have exactly the hypotheses of that node: the degree bound is imposed on every reduced subcurve, with no assumption of irreducibility or of characteristic zero. The section is nonzero on each generic point, and every nonempty $T\subseteq S$ satisfies $h^0(I_TL)+h^1(I_TL)<h^0(L)$.

source.place: Theorem 4.2, choice of a generic hyperplane section and last sentence, invoking Proposition 4.1.

proof.text: Consider $p:V\otimes_kV\to H^0(S,L^{\otimes2}|_S)$, $a\otimes b\mapsto (ab)|_S$. If $p$ is not surjective, [lem-sfb-cluster-product-obstruction] gives a nonempty $T\subseteq S$ with $h^0(I_TL)+h^1(I_TL)\geq h^0(L)+h^1(L)=h^0(L)$, contradicting Step 4. Thus $p$ is surjective. If $S$ is empty the target is zero and this conclusion holds directly.

source.place: Theorem 4.2, final sentence, invoking Lemma 2.12 and Proposition 4.1.

proof.text:
Locally write $L=\mathcal O_Xe$ and $s=ae$. Since $s$ has reduced smooth zero scheme and is nonzero at every component generic point, $a$ is a non-zero-divisor: it is a unit away from $S$, and at a point of $S$ it generates the maximal ideal of a smooth one-dimensional local ring. Equivalently, $X$ is reduced and a function vanishing on no component is a non-zero-divisor, as follows by embedding each affine reduced coordinate ring into the product of its component domains. From [def-pc-zero-scheme] the ideal of $S$ is locally $(a)$, so multiplication by $s$ identifies $I_S\otimes L\cong\mathcal O_X$ and gives
$$0\longrightarrow L\xrightarrow{s}L^{\otimes2}\longrightarrow Q\longrightarrow0,$$
where $Q$ is the module sheaf of $L^{\otimes2}|_S$ extended by zero. Local exactness is the sequence $0\to A\xrightarrow{a}A\to A/(a)\to0$. Its global sections are $H^0(S,L^{\otimes2}|_S)$.

source.place: Theorem 4.2, proof of exactness of the second row and surjectivity of the first column in the displayed diagram.

proof.text:
Step 2 and the cohomology sequence of Step 6 give
$$0\to H^0(X,L)\xrightarrow{s}H^0(X,L^{\otimes2})\to H^0(S,L^{\otimes2}|_S)\to0.$$
For $q\in H^0(X,L^{\otimes2})$, Step 5 supplies a finite sum $\sum_i a_ib_i$ with the same restriction as $q$. Exactness writes $q-\sum_i a_ib_i=sc$ for a global section $c$ of $L$. This expresses $q$ as a sum of quadratic products, proving the degree-two assertion.

source.place: Theorem 4.2, the diagram chase, written on sections.

proof.text: Choose $t\in V$ nonvanishing at every point of the finite set $S$. Each vanishing condition is a proper linear hyperplane since $L$ is generated (Step 3). A finite union of proper linear subspaces cannot exhaust a finite-dimensional vector space over the infinite field $k$: choose for each subspace a nonzero annihilating linear form; their product is a nonzero polynomial, and induction on the number of variables shows such a polynomial cannot vanish on every $k$-point. Thus such $t$ exists. The sections $s,t$ generate $L$ everywhere, because $s$ generates away from $S$ and $t$ generates at $S$.

source.place: Theorem 4.2, higher-degree multiplication assertion; explicit base-point-free pencil argument replacing the reference to Franciosi [8], Proposition 1.5.

proof.text:
The sheaf maps $L^{-1}\to\mathcal O_X^{\oplus2}\to L$ given by $c\mapsto(-tc,sc)$ and $(a,b)\mapsto sa+tb$ form a short exact sequence. Locally one of the coefficients of $s,t$ is a unit; solving $sa+tb=0$ then gives uniquely $(a,b)=(-tc,sc)$, which proves both injectivity and the kernel assertion. Tensor with $L^{\otimes n}$ to get
$$0\to L^{\otimes(n-1)}\to (L^{\otimes n})^{\oplus2}\xrightarrow{(s,t)}L^{\otimes(n+1)}\to0.$$
The same unit calculation proves exactness after tensoring. For $n\geq2$, Step 2 gives $H^1(X,L^{\otimes(n-1)})=0$, so its cohomology sequence makes $H^0(X,L^{\otimes n})^{\oplus2}\to H^0(X,L^{\otimes(n+1)})$ surjective. Its image consists of sums $su+tv$, hence lies in the image of $V\otimes H^0(X,L^{\otimes n})$.

source.place: Theorem 4.2, higher-degree assertion; explicit pencil-kernel computation and cohomology sequence.

proof.text: Induct on $j\geq1$ with the claim that every section of $L^{\otimes j}$ is a finite sum of products of $j$ sections of $L$. The case $j=1$ is the identity and $j=2$ is Step 7. If $j\geq2$, Step 9 writes any section in degree $j+1$ as $su+tv$; substitute the inductive product expressions for $u,v$. Thus the tensor multiplication is surjective in every degree. The multiplication of [def-sc-invertible-section-ring] is commutative, so each such product is the image of its monomial in $\operatorname{Sym}^j_kV$. This proves the required surjectivity without dividing by $j!$, in every characteristic.

source.place: Theorem 4.2, assembly of degree two with the higher-degree multiplication maps.

The item statement is unchanged and is Franciosi-Tenni Theorem 4.2 (p.49), specialised to connected nodal curves in any characteristic. I read the author PDF online because no local copy exists (WANTED); the source checks were Lemma 2.12 (pp.42-43), Prop 4.1 (pp.47-49), Thm 4.2 (p.49) and Section 2 (any characteristic), plus Stacks 0E3E verbatim. Steps 2-3: 0E3E with Z empty gives degree <= 2p_a-2, and with a reduced closed point gives <= 2p_a-1. Both contradict deg >= 2p_a+1, which gives H^1(L^r)=0 for r>=1 and that L is generated by global sections. p_a(B)>=0 comes from 0BUG. Advisory: (L^r)|_B=(L|_B)^r is used without a citation, a one-line identity. Steps 6-7 write the source's diagram chase out on sections. Steps 8-10 are a complete Castelnuovo base-point-free pencil argument replacing the source's [8, Prop 1.5]: n>=2 uses H^1(L^{n-1})=0, n=1 goes through degree 2, and there is no division by j!. New node lem-sfb-cluster-product-obstruction is Lemma 2.12 for a reduced smooth-support cluster with the restricted-line target; I checked it independently: a minimal failing T carries a full-support functional, so the image of V is isotropic for a nondegenerate diagonal form, giving 2c>=|T| in every characteristic. New node lem-sfb-general-section-cluster-strict-bound is Prop 4.1 plus the generic smooth reduced section from the proof of Thm 4.2. The worker's exclusion of the empty cluster is a correct fix: the printed statement gives equality there. I tested it on two P^1s meeting in one node with bidegree (1,1) and in two nodes with bidegree (1,2); every nonempty T gives a strict inequality. Both new nodes are statement-only and searched, and neither duplicates anything: lem-sfb-nodal-special-clifford-subcurve, 0E3E, lem-sfb-product-subseries-eventual-fullness and the other DAG grep hits are different statements. Their closure reaches only def-trf-schematically-dense-open, and the parent already cites all three, so I accept them. I accept all 14 declared tool_uses. lean.statement: theorem nodal_numerical_section_multiplication (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsHProjective f] [ConnectedSpace X] [IsReduced X] (hpure : X.IsPureDimension 1) (hnodal : ∀ x : X, x ∉ f.smoothLocus → ∃ e : AdicCompletion (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x) ≃+* (MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) k ⧸ Ideal.span {(MvPowerSeries.X 0 : MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) k) * (MvPowerSeries.X 1 : MvPowerSeries (Fin 2) k)}), ∀ a : k, e (AdicCompletion.of (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (X.presheaf.stalk x)) (X.presheaf.stalk x) (X.presheaf.germ ⊤ x trivial (f.appTop ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv a)))) = Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (MvPowerSeries.C a)) (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (hdegree : ∀ (B : Scheme.{u}) (i : B ⟶ X), IsClosedImmersion i → IsReduced B → Nonempty B → (∃ S : Set (Set X), S ⊆ irreducibleComponents X ∧ Set.range i = ⋃₀ S) → 2 * (1 - @Scheme.Modules.eulerChar k _ B ⟨i ≫ f⟩ (SheafOfModules.unit B.ringCatSheaf)) + 1 ≤ @Scheme.Modules.degree k _ B ⟨i ≫ f⟩ ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback i).obj L)) : ∀ j : ℕ, 1 ≤ j → ∃! μ : SymmetricPower k (ULift.{u} (Fin j)) ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom).obj (L.val.obj (Opposite.op ⊤))) →ₗ[k] ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom).obj ((L.tensorPow j).val.obj (Opposite.op ⊤))), (∀ s : ULift.{u} (Fin j) → ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop).hom).obj (L.val.obj (Opposite.op ⊤))), μ (SymmetricPower.tprod k s) = (∏ i : ULift.{u} (Fin j), (DirectSum.of (Scheme.Modules.SectionRingComponent L) 1 ((ρ_ L).inv.app ⊤ (s i)) : Scheme.Modules.InvertibleSectionRing L)) j) ∧ Function.Surjective μ
lean.note: The canonical symmetric multiplication is specified by its values on every pure symmetric tensor, as a uniquely specified surjective linear map; no arbitrary map is assumed. Products are evaluated in the existing InvertibleSectionRing. ULift (Fin j) only lifts the finite index set into the coefficient universe.
